description:
Advances: ancora.findings, ancora.gate

Findings: F5 (High, data H1 + spec H1, consensus CF2), F16 rides along (Medium, idioms M7 + simplicity M3). Consensus CF2 in ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
lib/ancora/trailer.ex:71-84 folds `git log <base>..HEAD` output (newest first) with Map.merge(acc, new), so when two commits acknowledge the same code at different severities the OLDEST commit wins. non_tip_overrides is then computed by dropping keys the tip mentions rather than by comparing applied values, so the code is excluded regardless of which severity won. Reproduced: tip declares derived/drift=warning, an older commit declares info; Trailer.read returns info with empty non_tip_overrides; the gate prints result=pass with no warning; after squash the tree resolves warning and fails on trunk. That is the post-merge verdict flip ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments exists to prevent, with the warning ancora-sfu added suppressed by construction. Neither ancora.findings.trailer_grammar nor ancora.gate.acknowledgment_clears defines precedence for the same code across commits, so it is a spec defect first and a code defect second.
Fix: reverse the fold so the commit nearest HEAD wins; compute non_tip_overrides by applied severity (keep a code when its winning value differs from what the tip supplies, or when the tip does not name it); replace the second Severity.resolve_all/2 pass in Gate.warn_non_tip_acknowledgments (gate.ex:494-508) with the direct check that the applied trailer value is what differs (F16; the second resolution is the duplication the simplicity and idioms reviewers both named). Define the precedence rule in the spec.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/trailer_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate through real git fixtures and the real CLI:
  1. Tip warning, older info, same code: the gate resolves warning; result reflects warning; no squash-loss warning (nothing would be lost). Mutation: restore the fold direction; the test must fail.
  2. Tip silent, older info, config or default stricter: the gate resolves info AND prints the squash-loss warning; after squash the trunk run resolves the stricter value. Mutation: compute non_tip_overrides by key; the test must fail.
  3. The four states from ancora-sfu (equal config silent, stricter config loud, no config loud, tip repeat silent) still hold byte-for-byte on stderr. Mutation: delete the F16 replacement and the old conjunction together; at least one must fail.
- Spec edit required in-diff: ancora.findings.trailer_grammar shall state that when the same code is acknowledged in more than one commit of the range, the commit nearest HEAD wins; ancora.gate.acknowledgment_clears gains a scenario for conflicting severities across commits (given/when/then with concrete values). Decision-record edit: ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments Decision or Consequences section records the precedence.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: Trailer.read/2 is called from Gate.check/2 (and Status); prove through the CLI fixtures and the gate test, not the trailer unit test alone.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/config.ex (F7 is another child), lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/git/**, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/mix/tasks/**
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/severity.ex (only if the applied-value comparison needs a helper)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (warn_non_tip_acknowledgments and its call site only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.durable_acknowledgments.md
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- The trailer grammar stays info|warning only, no off, no presets. No announcement of tip-commit acknowledgments (F41, deferred). Do not read the merge commit body. Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

Summary: Trailer.read now gives the commit nearest HEAD precedence and retains the nearest differing below-tip value, while Gate warns only when that below-tip value supplied the finding severity and differs from durable config or the default. Mutation proof: item 1's oldest-wins fold produced 1 failure from 1 selected CLI test and passed 1 of 1 after revert; item 2's key-based non-tip filter produced 1 failure from 1 selected trailer test and passed 1 of 1 after revert; item 3's old source-and-membership predicate produced 2 failures from 2 selected CLI tests and passed 2 of 2 after revert. The final 67-test run passed and pins equal config silent, stricter config loud, no config loud, and tip repeat silent byte-for-byte on stderr.

TEST_CRITIC: FAIL

Blocking: the nearest-below-tip ordering introduced by this diff's own must-level spec edit has no covering test, and its failure mode is the ticket's own bug.

FAILING ITEM

lib/ancora/trailer.ex non_tip fold, second `Enum.reverse()`: no test in the repo has two conflicting below-tip trailer commits. Every fixture in test/ancora/trailer_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs and test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs carries exactly one below-tip commit that names a code, so the below-tip fold direction is never discriminated.

ancora.findings.trailer_grammar (priority: must) now states the read result "shall identify the nearest valid value below the tip". Delete that second `Enum.reverse()` and `overrides` still resolves nearest while `non_tip_overrides` reverts to oldest-wins. Fixture: C1 `Spec-Ack: derived/drift=warning`, C2 `Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info`, C3 tip with no trailer, default severity error. finding.severity resolves :info from the nearest; non_tip_severity becomes :warning from the oldest; the gate's `finding.severity == non_tip_severity` conjunct goes false; the squash-loss warning is suppressed and the trunk run after squash flips to error. That is F5 one layer down, and the full suite stays green.

Missing test: a CLI fixture with two conflicting below-tip acknowledgments and a bare tip, asserting `stderr == @squash_warning` on the branch and the stricter resolution after squash.

UNVERIFIED BY READING: that the suppression actually reaches stderr under this mutation. Mutation for the verifier: drop `Enum.reverse()` from the `non_tip_overrides` pipeline in lib/ancora/trailer.ex (keep the one in `overrides`); expect 0 failures across the three named files.

PER-ASSERTION VERDICT

1. "the tip acknowledgment wins when commits name conflicting severities" (spec_check_test.exs:385) PASS. Commits are built older-first: `Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info` on the earlier commit, `=warning` on the tip. Trailer.read reads `git log <base>..HEAD` (newest first), so List.first is genuinely the tip. Resolved severity asserted by equality off the JSON report (`drift["severity"] == "warning"`, `severity_source == "trailer"`), status 1, last stdout line pinned in full, and `stderr == "** (Mix) spec.check failed\n"` by equality so any squash-loss line breaks it. Under the old oldest-wins fold this resolves info, status 0, verdict pass: three assertions fail.

2. "a non-tip acknowledgment changes the result after squash" (spec_check_test.exs:415) PASS on structure. It creates a real `feature` branch, commits the info trailer below a bare tip, runs the real CLI, then `git checkout main`, `git merge --squash feature`, a real trunk commit with no trailer, and re-runs the CLI against the same `--base`. Branch half: severity info / source trailer by equality, `stderr == @squash_warning` byte-for-byte. Trunk half: severity error / source default by equality, errors=1, `stderr == "** (Mix) spec.check failed\n"`. Real squash, real re-run.

3. "repeating the non-tip acknowledgment on the tip stays silent" (spec_check_test.exs:460) PASS. This is the genuine tip-repeat-at-the-same-severity state, which existed nowhere before: the pre-existing trailer unit test claimed it by name but its fixture used differing severities. `stderr == ""` is the behavioral guard on the `Map.reject` equal-value drop; remove that reject and the warning fires and this fails.

4. trailer_test.exs:154 "the nearest override wins and keeps a differing non-tip value" PARTIAL. It pins nearest-wins (`overrides["derived/drift"] == :info` with earlier=warning, tip=info) and differing-retained (`non_tip_overrides == %{"derived/drift" => :warning}`). It does NOT pin the equal-dropped half. That half is guarded only behaviorally by CLI item 3 above. Non-blocking, but the unit test does not pin both halves as the ticket asked.

5. Key-based non_tip mutation: it fails ONLY trailer_test.exs:154. None of the three CLI tests catches it, and none can. Under nearest-wins the two computations are gate-indistinguishable. When the tip names the code, value-based keeps a differing below-tip value but the gate's `finding.severity == non_tip_severity` conjunct is then false, so silent; key-based drops it, also silent. When the tip omits the code, both keep it. So the ticket's item-2 mutation is proven by a unit assertion on a returned map, not "through real git fixtures and the real CLI" as the ticket framed it. Worth knowing: the differing-value retention has no observable consequence at the gate today.

6. No weakening of the ancora-sfu tests. Name-list diff of e18fa05 vs a56fd93 shows zero tests removed and zero fixtures altered. Four assertions were TIGHTENED: `unpromoted.stderr =~ "lost by a squash merge"` and the two `refute ... =~` became `== @squash_warning` / `== ""`, and the higher-severity test likewise. Ordered unpromoted / promoted / trunk and the stricter-config case are intact.

7. No assertion pins source text. `@squash_warning` pins subprocess stderr, which is the ancora.tasks.stderr_pinning contract. The pre-existing moduledoc assertion in trailer_test.exs is untouched by this diff.

8. Reachability of the subprocess stderr assertions is VERIFIED, not assumed. `run_mix_subprocess` writes a shell wrapper redirecting fd 2 to a file. Positive (`== @squash_warning`) and negative (`== ""`) assertions coexist in the same file and both pass, so a silently-empty capture would fail the positive ones.

RUNS

test/ancora/gate_test.exs: 32 tests, 0 failures.
